title: Tree-Guided Identify-Then-Exploit: A Unified Framework of Best Arm Identification and Regret Minimization for Dueling Bandits
claim: Arms decompose along an ancestor path into geometrically growing sibling blocks whose sizes sum to N-1, which keeps total cost linear.
layout: 1 panel, top-down binary tree, left-to-right levels, brace with sum equation
description: A single top-down tree diagram. Gray rounded boxes on the left form the ancestor path: root = U_L(b) at level L, then U_{L-1}(b), U_{L-2}(b), a vertical ellipsis, U_1(b), and {b} at level 0. Gray level labels (level L, L-1, ..., 0) sit to the left of each box. From each ancestor box, a gray arrow points down-left to the next ancestor and a navy arrow points down-right to a dashed, lavender sibling block Q_L(b), Q_{L-1}(b), and so on down to Q_1(b). Navy annotations beside the blocks read 2^{L-1} arms, 2^{L-2} arms, and 1 arm. A large navy curly brace on the right, with the equation sum_h |Q_h| = N-1, spans the blocks. A legend at the top right maps the gray box to the ancestor path and the dashed lavender box to sibling blocks. The eye goes first to the root and then follows the staircase down.
caption: The ancestor path of a starting arm $b$ decomposes the arms into sibling blocks $Q_1(b),\ldots,Q_L(b)$. TreeAscent walks up the ancestor path, runs a knockout tournament on each sibling block to obtain a representative, and merges that representative with the current champion. If a block contains $a^\star$, the representative is $a^\star$ with high probability. Block sizes grow geometrically ($|Q_h|=2^{h-1}$), enabling a size-proportional confidence allocation that keeps the total identification cost linear in $N$.
abstract: We study $N$-armed stochastic dueling bandits under the Condorcet-winner assumption with a positive global gap, where three widely adopted objectives are considered: best-arm identification (BAI), weak regret, and strong regret. We propose Tree-Guided Identify-Then-Exploit (TG-ITE), the first unified framework to tackle all these objectives to our knowledge. Without requiring transitivity assumptions, we propose a shared tree-guided identification approach to find a high-confidence incumbent within $O(N)$ comparisons. We further propose varied exploitation strategies to utilize this warm-start stage to optimize the specific objectives at hand. For a fixed global gap $Î$, this methodology enables our approach to (1) build the first winner-stays-style algorithm to achieve $O(N)$ weak regret; (2) realize the joint optimization of BAI and weak regret with $O(N)$ guarantees for both, eliminating the sub-optimal $O(\log N)$ factors of the existing approach; (3) attain the same $O(N\log T)$ order as specialized strong-regret approaches; and (4) achieve $O(N)$ sample complexity in BAI, matching a worst-case lower bound up to an additional $\log(1/Î)$ term. If a lower bound on the minimal winner gap is known, this term can be removed. Our results suggest that a single identification primitive can serve BAI and both regret objectives with linear dependence on $N$.
